name: Duke Bootee
hook: Wrote and largely performed the most important rap record of its era, which was released under a group name he was not in.
blurb: Ed Fletcher, who called himself Duke Bootee, was a percussionist in Sugar Hill Records' house band. In 1980 he wrote a song about the daily grind of city life, set during a New York transit strike. It came out in 1982 as 'The Message' by Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five, the record where rap's subject opens out from parties and boasting to the conditions people lived in. Bootee wrote it, co-produced it with Clifton Chase, and performs a large share of it: of the Furious Five, only Melle Mel took part, and the rest of the voice is Bootee's own. Flash had nothing to do with it, so the record carries the name of a group Bootee was not in and of a DJ who was not in the room. That is the clearest example on this map of the gap between who makes a record and whose name is on it. He is one of the most important writers in the music and one of the least known.
